title: promotion-receipt/v0 record
description: DRAFT (draft_revision 2) -- NOT FROZEN. A promotion-receipt is a machine-evaluated, deterministic (zero LLM calls) verdict over every predicate EXCEPT human approval: 'ready_for_approval | ineligible | abstained'. It carries NO promotion authority by itself -- authority is release-approval/v0's event, which binds to this receipt's exact digest. Naming: this contract deliberately does NOT use the word 'decision' anywhere in its fields (see docs/protocols/promotion-receipt-v0.md) to avoid collision with the unrelated contracts/decision/v1 (a human design-decision record); this contract's outcome field is `verdict`. See docs/protocols/promotion-receipt-v0.md.

evaluation_phase.description: R11: which predicate_id closed set applies. pre_promotion and post_deploy predicates are never mixed in the same receipt (schema-enforced below).

bundle_digest.description: The release-evidence/v0 bundle this receipt evaluates. Not recomputed by THIS contract's own verifier (no bundle is carried alongside a bare receipt fixture) -- release-approval/v0's composite ledger fixture is where a receipt's subject.bundle_digest is cross-checked against a real bundle/approval chain.

selection_manifest_digest.description: OPAQUE in v0: the selection-manifest contract this digest points at does not exist yet (open question in the source plan, sol Round 3). Consumers define its shape and how to recompute it; this contract only pins the value. See docs/protocols/promotion-receipt-v0.md caveat.

policy_digest.description: Frozen at evaluation start, same as effective_risk (R4/sol Round 2: a receipt never re-derives risk or policy from its own evaluation result -- that would be a self-consistency loop).

independence_policy_digest.description: draft_revision 2: JCS sha256 of the frozen independence policy (policy/independence-policy.json) this receipt's independence checks were evaluated under. Distinct from policy_digest: policy_digest names the general promotion policy (opaque here); independence_policy_digest names exactly the (effective_risk, predicate_id) -> acceptable {code, attestation} set. The verifier recomputes the digest of the policy it was given and rejects any mismatch -- a syntactically valid digest is not a binding by itself.

promotion_id.description: draft_revision 2: the promotion run this receipt belongs to. The verifier rejects a receipt whose promotion_id differs from the caller-supplied expected_promotion_id (in production, the calling workflow fixes it -- never read from the receipt itself), and the session ledger is resolved in the EXPECTED promotion_id's namespace.

session_ledger_digest.description: draft_revision 2: JCS sha256 of the orchestrator session ledger (orchestrator-session-ledger.schema.json) for this promotion_id, or null when the evaluator had no ledger. A resolved ledger whose digest differs is rejected; an unresolvable ledger makes every orchestrator_observed attestation evaluate to unknown -- never satisfied.

effective_risk.description: The value frozen AT THE START of this evaluation -- recorded, not recomputed from the verdict.

semantic_digest.description: R12: sha256 of the JCS canonical bytes of this receipt with evaluated_at, receipt_id, and semantic_digest itself removed. Recomputed by the verifier; a mismatch is rejected. Used for TOCTOU identity comparison -- time is deliberately excluded.

predicate_id.description: R11 closed set (pre_promotion: artifact_identity, review_admissibility, verification_coverage, preview_verified, rollback_target_valid, privilege_boundary; post_deploy: deployed_artifact_readback). human_release_approval is deliberately absent from this enum -- it is never a predicate (R11), it is release-approval/v0's own event.

kind.description: review_finding: ref is "<review-findings record_id>#<finding_id>" (an actual finding in that record) or "<record_id>#scope" (only valid when that record's outcome is none_observed_in_recorded_scope); digest MUST equal the WHOLE record's JCS (RFC 8785) sha256 -- its record_digest, NOT subject.digest (R23 -- editing a finding's claim/severity/outcome changes record_digest even when subject.digest, bound to the scanned tree, stays the same; a finding recorded against a stale record_digest cannot back a predicate about the current content, TEST-12). release_evidence: ref is a release_id, digest is the release-evidence/v0 bundle's own JCS sha256 (resolved by digest against embedded bundles in release-approval/v0's composite fixture, not by release_id alone -- one release_id can have multiple attempts at different digests). other: opaque, this contract's verifier does not resolve it.

verdict.description: R13: closed to exactly these three. 'eligible' and 'break_glass_authorized' do not exist in this schema at all -- eligible was Round-5-retired for an authority circularity (a receipt cannot itself grant promotion eligibility, only say 'ready for a human to approve'), and break-glass is release-approval/v0's own event kind, never a receipt verdict.

independenceCheck.description: draft_revision 2: per (predicate_id x evidence_ref) independence check. REQUIRED on every evidence_ref of an applicable predicate that has a rule in the frozen independence policy for this receipt's effective_risk, and FORBIDDEN everywhere else (the not_applicable half is schema-enforced; the policy-dependent half is enforced by evaluate.mjs). `required` is the policy rule's acceptable set copied verbatim (same order); `observed` is {code, verified attestation} derived from the referenced review-findings record (null for any evidence kind other than review_finding); `check` is derived, never asserted: unknown attestation -> unknown; principal-class code -> unknown; technical code -> satisfied iff {code, attestation} is in required, else unsatisfied. unsatisfied -> ineligible, unknown -> abstained, unsatisfied wins when mixed. Every field is recomputed by the verifier and a mismatch is rejected.
